minutes.headline: Historical Commission approved demolition of 11 The Clearing as not significant, and backed pushing CPA adoption again.
minutes.summary: Remote meeting of the Lunenburg Historical Commission. The commission approved the prior minutes, voted unanimously to let the demolition at 11 The Clearing proceed, and heard updates on the Primary School reuse research, the demolition delay bylaw amendments, cemetery work, and a renewed Community Preservation Act effort. No formal vote was taken on CPA or the endangered list.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment; the only member of the public present, Bill Tyler, had none.

votes.motion: Accept the minutes of the December 17, 2020 meeting as read
votes.outcome: passed (roll call, all members voting aye as heard)

votes.motion: Recommend the demolition application for 11 The Clearing be approved and demolition proceed at the owner's convenience

budget_items.topic: Arnold Litchfield memorial tree removal quote
budget_items.what_was_said: One quote for tree work had been received for the memorial site.
A member cited the renovation of Fitchburg's city hall as a parallel for the Primary School.

budget_items.topic: Cemetery commission FY22 budget for stone
budget_items.what_was_said: Cemetery funds in the next fiscal year's budget cover purchasing stones, available after July 1.
Members discussed CPA matching funds for historic projects, and that real estate transactions in town pay in without the town drawing funds back.
Other communities used historic grants, state and federal funds, CPA funds and housing authority grants to rehab similar buildings.

decisions.decision: Members will informally look at K houses from the 1833 map as they travel, before a professional survey, as a start toward an endangered list.
The commission will first develop its own town survey plan; the chair and Bill Laxo to review the consultant's response and outline it for the next meeting.
If the demolition delay amendments miss the annual town meeting warrant, they will be sought for the fall special town meeting.
Chair to contact other commissions and boards to build consensus to promote the CPA to the select board.
Next meeting set for Thursday March 25 at 7 p.m.

what_happened.line: The Historical Commission voted unanimously to recommend approval of the demolition application for 11 The Clearing, letting demolition proceed at the owner's convenience.
Members agreed to seek the demolition delay bylaw amendments at the fall special town meeting if they miss the annual town meeting warrant.
The chair will contact other commissions and boards to build consensus for promoting the Community Preservation Act to the select board; no vote was taken.
Members will informally look at houses from the 1833 map as a start toward an endangered list, and will first draft their own town survey plan.
The commission approved the December 17, 2020 minutes and set its next meeting for Thursday, March 25, at 7 p.m.

why_it_matters: The Community Preservation Act, if adopted, would add a local funding source for historic projects such as reusing the Primary School, and adopting it is a vote residents would be asked to take.
The demolition delay bylaw amendments would change how long a historic building waits before it can be torn down, and they need a town meeting article to take effect.
